title: fix: recover historical agent KPI from run tokens
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Replaces the Agent volume with observed top-level runs, keeping the runs/users switch and MCP unchanged.
- Uses existing verified ag_ parent-request links; deduplicates request IDs and excludes nested runs and runs without recorded child calls.
- Handles Sunday-to-Monday child calls; leaves weeks before August 24 unavailable and explains coverage in tooltips/CSV labels.
- Passes 36 dashboard tests, the production build, and real Tinybird SQL fixtures covering duplicates, nesting, week boundaries and missing data. Live historical queries return counts for both requested weeks.
- Main-only change. Rollout requires staging-first Tinybird deployment before the KPI production deployment; no datasource or secret changes.

gist.headline: The KPI found its roots
gist.blurb: The agent chart was counting the right kind of work in the wrong shape. It now follows verified parent requests, so the historical garden has fewer duplicate sprouts.
gist.summary: Reworked the weekly Agent KPI to count deduplicated observed top-level runs through verified ag_ parent-request links, excluding nested runs and runs without recorded child calls while preserving the runs/users switch and MCP metric.
gist.impact: The internal KPI dashboard now returns historical agent-run counts for requested weeks, correctly carrying Sunday-to-Monday child calls across week boundaries and clearly marking coverage before August 24 as unavailable.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy observability garden where Polli traces verified parent-request roots from a top-level run into a tidy weekly chart; duplicate and nested sprouts are gently pruned, while a small calendar bridge carries a child-call flower from Sunday into Monday. A CRT monitor robot can display the corrected run count, with code-plants and a subtle unavailable section of the historical garden reinforcing data coverage.
